expectations.text: The bottom line clearly AGREES that adding a unique constraint/index on email is the right move (a plain yes, possibly with caveats), rather than rejecting or hedging it.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**Verdict: yes, add it.**" and "**Bottom line:** do it, but with case-insensitive matching, built concurrently, after you merge the existing duplicates, and with the app handling the new error." | grader 2: "Verdict: yes, add it." and "Bottom line: do it, but with case-insensitive matching..."

expectations.text: Addresses case-insensitive uniqueness (e.g. a unique index on lower(email), or citext).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Uniqueness is case-sensitive by default. A plain unique index treats `Bob@x.com` and `bob@x.com` as different emails" with Option A (normalize on write) and Option B (expression index on `lower(email)`), and the suggested `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uniq ON users (lower(email));` | grader 2: "Uniqueness is case-sensitive by default... Option A: normalize on write... Option B: an expression index on lower(email)"

expectations.text: Says existing duplicate rows must be found and resolved before the unique index can be built.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "The build will fail on your existing duplicates... Find them first:" followed by the GROUP BY/HAVING count(*) > 1 query and "Merging them is the real work"; suggested order step 2 "Find and merge the duplicates" before step 3 "Build the index". | grader 2: "The build will fail on your existing duplicates... Find them first" with a SQL query, plus step 2 in Suggested order: "Find and merge the duplicates... before Build the index" (step 3)

expectations.text: Recommends building the index without blocking writes (e.g. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) or otherwise addresses locking on a ~4M-row table.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "A plain `CREATE INDEX` blocks writes... Use `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`" plus caveats on transactions, INVALID index on failure, and waiting for long-running transactions. | grader 2: "A plain CREATE INDEX blocks writes... Use CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and know what comes with it" plus the example SQL uses CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY

expectations.text: Mentions handling the unique-violation error / race at signup in the application.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "After this change, a signup race raises Postgres error `23505` (unique violation) instead of creating a duplicate. Catch it and treat it as 'account already exists', or use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`." | grader 2: "a signup race raises Postgres error 23505 (unique violation) instead of creating a duplicate. Catch it and treat it as 'account already exists', or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id"

expectations.text: Does not manufacture a blocking objection to the core proposal.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: All objections are framed as prerequisites or caveats to doing it ("do it, but..."); the dissent section notes the index may not cover different-email duplicates but does not argue against adding it. | grader 2: Dissent section raises real caveats (different-email accounts, email squatting, Gmail dots/+tags) but explicitly concludes 'do it' rather than rejecting the index; no objection is framed as a reason not to add it
